correctness.rationale: The normalized ambiguity formula follows from Gaussian integration. Disk reduction follows from strict radial decay. The angular sum is strictly decreasing in cos(6 phi), by a negative third derivative and a divided-difference formula. Averaging at the three minimizing axes bounds every weight allocation, with equality only for equal weights when squeezed. The scalar threshold map C(u) increases from 2 to infinity because (1+2y)log(y)<(y-1)(y+2) for y>1; this gives the unique global maximum. Taylor expansion and the exponentially fast convergence of the stationary equation give the two asymptotic regimes. Standalone code ran 99 finite symbolic/grid/asymptotic checks; the analytical inequalities, not the grid, establish universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: Weighted squared ambiguity is exactly the natural pointwise information multiplier under independent unit-precision ambiguity observations. An exact global design is useful because a squeeze that improves directional coverage can reduce coverage near the origin. The theorem determines a non-obvious sharp disk-radius threshold, unique post-threshold allocation and dilation, cubic onset, and a limiting universal squeeze sqrt(3), together with an exponentially improved worst-case multiplier at large radius. These distinctions supply quantitative design criteria not reducible to merely writing down a Gaussian integral or relabeling a known result; they do not require a general nonlinear stability theorem.
